newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak SAX index slips 0.17 pts in flat trading.
newsitem.headline: Slovak SAX index slips 0.17 pts in flat trading.

text.p: Major Slovak shares were mixed in flat trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Friday, with a drop to Nafta shares dragging the SAX index down 0.17 points to 186.21.
Oil and gas storage company Nafta fell 60 crowns to 1,690, while steel maker VSZ dominated activity on the BSE's listed floor, closing up eight crowns at 650.

"Friday's drop in Nafta had quite fundamental reasons, as the share did not trade for some five days," said Dusan Sykora of ING Barings. "It may decrease even further in near future, as the blocks offered in Nafta for trade are at even lower prices at the moment."
Brokers said foreign investor interest was still too weak to create an expected uptrend on the bourse.
"I see no major change in the trend from the short-term point of view. But I expect it (the bourse) to edge up after some time, as some prices seem pretty attractive at the moment," Sykora said.
Oil refinery Slovnaft, closed unchanged at 800 crowns,
Overall volume, boosted mainly by blcok trades, increased to 631,968 shares, from 181,558 shares traded on Thursday, while turnover rose to 280.7 million crowns, from 87.46 million.
